title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

requirements.stmt: A memory bank must be built from the word-level embeddings of all tokens in the normal training documents only (no anomalous-token embeddings are stored).

requirements.stmt: The token-level anomaly score is the minimum distance from the test-token embedding to any memory-bank entry (Equation 2); larger distance means more anomalous.

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")

   71|         return scores

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7|

    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|

import json
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple


def load_grammar() -> List[Dict]:
    npy_path = 'repo/data/grammar.npy'
    json_path = 'repo/data/grammar_correction_labeled.json'
    
    npy = np.load(npy_path, allow_pickle=True)
    data = npy.item() if npy.ndim == 0 else npy
    sentences = data['sentences']   # list of list of str (usually one string per doc)
    tokens = data['tokens']         # list of list of str
    labels = data['labels']         # list of list of int
    
    with open(json_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        json_docs = json.load(f)
    
    assert len(sentences) == 300, f"Expected 300 docs, got {len(sentences)}"
    assert len(tokens) == 300
    assert len(labels) == 300
    assert len(json_docs) == 300
    
    docs = []
    for i in range(300):
        text = json_docs[i]['data']['text']
        doc_label = int(json_docs[i]['data']['label'])
        doc_tokens = tokens[i]
        doc_token_labels = [int(x) for x in labels[i]]
        
        # Consistency checks
        assert len(doc_tokens) == len(doc_token_labels), \
            f"Doc {i}: token/label length mismatch {len(doc_tokens)} vs {len(doc_token_labels)}"
        
        token_has_anomaly = any(x == 1 for x in doc_token_labels)
        if token_has_anomaly:
            assert doc_label == 1, f"Doc {i}: has anomalous token but doc_label=0"
        else:
            assert doc_label == 0, f"Doc {i}: no anomalous token but doc_label=1"
        
        docs.append({
            'id': i,
            'text': text,
            'tokens': doc_tokens,
            'token_labels': doc_token_labels,
            'doc_label': doc_label,
        })
    
    normal_docs = [d for d in docs if d['doc_label'] == 0]
    anomalous_docs = [d for d in docs if d['doc_label'] == 1]
    assert len(normal_docs) == 270, f"Expected 270 normal docs, got {len(normal_docs)}"
    assert len(anomalous_docs) == 30, f"Expected 30 anomalous docs, got {len(anomalous_docs)}"
    
    return docs, normal_docs, anomalous_docs


def split_docs(normal_docs: List[Dict], anomalous_docs: List[Dict], seed: int = 0) -> Tuple[List[Dict], List[Dict]]:
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    normal_shuffled = normal_docs.copy()
    rng.shuffle(normal_shuffled)
    
    n_train = len(normal_shuffled) // 2
    train_docs = normal_shuffled[:n_train]
    test_docs = normal_shuffled[n_train:] + anomalous_docs
    
    return train_docs, test_docs


if __name__ == '__main__':
    docs, normal_docs, anomalous_docs = load_grammar()
    train_docs, test_docs = split_docs(normal_docs, anomalous_docs, seed=0)
    
    print(f"Total docs: {len(docs)}")
    print(f"Normal docs: {len(normal_docs)}, Anomalous docs: {len(anomalous_docs)}")
    print(f"Train docs: {len(train_docs)} (all normal)")
    print(f"Test docs: {len(test_docs)} ({sum(1 for d in test_docs if d['doc_label']==0)} normal, {sum(1 for d in test_docs if d['doc_label']==1)} anomalous)")
    
    total_tokens = sum(len(d['tokens']) for d in docs)
    total_anom_tokens = sum(sum(d['token_labels']) for d in docs)
    print(f"Total tokens: {total_tokens}, anomalous tokens: {total_anom_tokens} ({100*total_anom_tokens/total_tokens:.2f}%)")
    
    test_tokens = sum(len(d['tokens']) for d in test_docs)
    test_anom_tokens = sum(sum(d['token_labels']) for d in test_docs)
    print(f"Test tokens: {test_tokens}, anomalous test tokens: {test_anom_tokens} ({100*test_anom_tokens/test_tokens:.2f}%)")

import torch
import numpy as np
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple
from tqdm import tqdm


def get_tokenizer_model(model_name: str = "bert-base-uncased", device: str = None):
    if device is None:
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = model.to(device).eval()
    return tokenizer, model, device


def embed_docs(
    docs: List[Dict],
    tokenizer,
    model,
    device: str,
    max_length: int = 128,
    batch_size: int = 32,
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Returns:
        embeddings: shape (n_docs, max_n_words, hidden_dim) padded with NaN
        word_masks: shape (n_docs, max_n_words) bool, True for real words
    """
    all_embeddings = []
    all_masks = []
    
    # Process one by one to keep alignment simple (short sentences)
    for doc in tqdm(docs, desc="Embedding docs"):
        tokens = doc['tokens']
        encoded = tokenizer(
            tokens,
            is_split_into_words=True,
            return_tensors="pt",
            truncation=True,
            max_length=max_length,
            padding=False,
        )
        input_ids = encoded["input_ids"].to(device)
        attention_mask = encoded["attention_mask"].to(device)
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask)
            last_hidden_state = outputs.last_hidden_state[0]  # (seq_len, hidden_dim)
        
        word_ids = encoded.word_ids(batch_index=0)
        
        # Collect subword embeddings per word
        word_embs = {}
        for pos, word_idx in enumerate(word_ids):
            if word_idx is None:
                continue
            emb = last_hidden_state[pos].cpu().numpy()
            if word_idx not in word_embs:
                word_embs[word_idx] = []
            word_embs[word_idx].append(emb)
        
        # Max pool subwords per word
        doc_word_embs = []
        for idx in range(len(tokens)):
            if idx in word_embs:
                stacked = np.stack(word_embs[idx], axis=0)
                pooled = np.max(stacked, axis=0)
                doc_word_embs.append(pooled)
            else:
                # Word was truncated or missing; skip
                pass
        
        all_embeddings.append(np.array(doc_word_embs, dtype=np.float32))
        all_masks.append(np.ones(len(doc_word_embs), dtype=bool))
    
    # Pad to same length
    max_words = max(emb.shape[0] for emb in all_embeddings)
    hidden_dim = all_embeddings[0].shape[1]
    
    padded_embeddings = np.full((len(docs), max_words, hidden_dim), np.nan, dtype=np.float32)
    padded_masks = np.zeros((len(docs), max_words), dtype=bool)
    
    for i, (emb, mask) in enumerate(zip(all_embeddings, all_masks)):
        n = emb.shape[0]
        padded_embeddings[i, :n] = emb
        padded_masks[i, :n] = mask
    
    return padded_embeddings, padded_masks


def flatten_masked(
    embeddings: np.ndarray,
    masks: np.ndarray,
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, List[Tuple[int, int]]]:
    """
    Flatten (n_docs, max_words, dim) -> (n_total_words, dim) using mask.
    Returns embeddings matrix and index list mapping each row to (doc_idx, word_idx).
    """
    rows = []
    indices = []
    for doc_idx in range(embeddings.shape[0]):
        for word_idx in range(embeddings.shape[1]):
            if masks[doc_idx, word_idx]:
                rows.append(embeddings[doc_idx, word_idx])
                indices.append((doc_idx, word_idx))
    return np.array(rows, dtype=np.float32), indices


if __name__ == '__main__':
    from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_docs
    docs, normal_docs, anomalous_docs = load_grammar()
    train_docs, test_docs = split_docs(normal_docs, anomalous_docs, seed=0)
    
    tokenizer, model, device = get_tokenizer_model()
    print(f"Device: {device}")
    
    train_emb, train_mask = embed_docs(train_docs, tokenizer, model, device)
    test_emb, test_mask = embed_docs(test_docs, tokenizer, model, device)
    
    print(f"Train embeddings: {train_emb.shape}, mask sum: {train_mask.sum()}")
    print(f"Test embeddings: {test_emb.shape}, mask sum: {test_mask.sum()}")
    
    # Check alignment
    train_flat, train_idx = flatten_masked(train_emb, train_mask)
    test_flat, test_idx = flatten_masked(test_emb, test_mask)
    print(f"Train flat: {train_flat.shape}")
    print(f"Test flat: {test_flat.shape}")
    
    # Verify no NaNs
    assert not np.isnan(train_flat).any(), "NaN in train embeddings"
    assert not np.isnan(test_flat).any(), "NaN in test embeddings"
    print("No NaNs found.")

import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple


def compute_token_metrics(
    token_scores: np.ndarray,
    token_labels: np.ndarray,
) -> Dict[str, float]:
    assert token_scores.shape[0] == token_labels.shape[0]
    assert token_labels.min() >= 0 and token_labels.max() <= 1
    
    auroc = roc_auc_score(token_labels, token_scores)
    auprc = average_precision_score(token_labels, token_scores)
    
    return {
        'token_auroc': float(auroc),
        'token_auprc': float(auprc),
        'n_tokens': int(token_labels.shape[0]),
        'n_positive_tokens': int(token_labels.sum()),
    }


def compute_doc_metrics(
    doc_scores: np.ndarray,
    doc_labels: np.ndarray,
) -> Dict[str, float]:
    assert doc_scores.shape[0] == doc_labels.shape[0]
    assert doc_labels.min() >= 0 and doc_labels.max() <= 1
    
    auroc = roc_auc_score(doc_labels, doc_scores)
    auprc = average_precision_score(doc_labels, doc_scores)
    
    return {
        'doc_auroc': float(auroc),
        'doc_auprc': float(auprc),
        'n_docs': int(doc_labels.shape[0]),

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import numpy as np

# Ensure src is importable
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))

from src.data_grammar import load_grammar, split_docs
from src.embed_bert import get_tokenizer_model, embed_docs, flatten_masked
from src.detector import fit_token_core, score_tokens
from src.evaluate import compute_token_metrics, compute_doc_metrics, aggregate_doc_scores, random_baseline


def run_grammar(seed: int = 0, smoke: bool = False):
    start = time.time()
    
    # Load data
    docs, normal_docs, anomalous_docs = load_grammar()
    
    if smoke:
        # Use tiny subset: 8 normal + 2 anomalous
        train_docs = normal_docs[:8]
        test_docs = normal_docs[8:10] + anomalous_docs[:2]
    else:
        train_docs, test_docs = split_docs(normal_docs, anomalous_docs, seed=seed)
    
    # Embed
    tokenizer, model, device = get_tokenizer_model()
    print(f"Device: {device}")
    
    train_emb, train_mask = embed_docs(train_docs, tokenizer, model, device)
    test_emb, test_mask = embed_docs(test_docs, tokenizer, model, device)
    
    # Flatten
    X_train, _ = flatten_masked(train_emb, train_mask)
    X_test, test_indices = flatten_masked(test_emb, test_mask)
    
    # Build gold labels for test tokens
    test_token_labels = []
    test_doc_labels = []
    doc_token_masks = []
    for doc_idx, doc in enumerate(test_docs):
        doc_token_masks.append(np.array([i[0] == doc_idx for i in test_indices]))
        test_token_labels.extend(doc['token_labels'])
        test_doc_labels.append(doc['doc_label'])
    test_token_labels = np.array(test_token_labels, dtype=int)
    test_doc_labels = np.array(test_doc_labels, dtype=int)
    
    # Sanity: train has no anomalous tokens
    train_token_labels = []
    for doc in train_docs:
        train_token_labels.extend(doc['token_labels'])
    assert all(l == 0 for l in train_token_labels), "Train set contains anomalous tokens!"
    
    # Fit and score
    model_tok = fit_token_core(X_train)
    token_scores = score_tokens(model_tok, X_test)
    
    # Training self-distance sanity (exclude self by adding small noise to avoid exact 0)
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    noise = rng.normal(0, 1e-6, X_train.shape).astype(np.float32)
    X_train_noisy = X_train + noise
    train_scores = score_tokens(model_tok, X_train_noisy)
    max_self_dist = float(np.max(train_scores))
    
    # Metrics
    token_metrics = compute_token_metrics(token_scores, test_token_labels)
    doc_scores = aggregate_doc_scores(token_scores, doc_token_masks)
    doc_metrics = compute_doc_metrics(doc_scores, test_doc_labels)
    rand_baseline = random_baseline(test_token_labels)
    
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    
    result = {
        'seed': seed,
        'dataset': 'grammar',
        'smoke': smoke,
        'device': device,
        'n_train_docs': len(train_docs),
        'n_test_docs': len(test_docs),
        'n_train_tokens': int(X_train.shape[0]),
        'n_test_tokens': int(X_test.shape[0]),
        'n_positive_test_tokens': int(test_token_labels.sum()),
        'max_self_distance_train': max_self_dist,
        **token_metrics,
        **doc_metrics,
        **rand_baseline,
        'elapsed_seconds': round(elapsed, 2),
    }
    
    return result


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--dataset', default='grammar')
    parser.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument('--smoke', action='store_true')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    if args.dataset != 'grammar':
        raise ValueError("Only grammar dataset is supported in this reproduction.")
    
    result = run_grammar(seed=args.seed, smoke=args.smoke)
    
    os.makedirs('results', exist_ok=True)
    with open('results/metrics.json', 'w') as f:
        json.dump(result, f, indent=2)
    
    print("\n=== Final Metrics ===")
    for k, v in result.items():
        print(f"{k}: {v}")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

from src.data_grammar import load_grammar, split_docs

from src.detector import fit_token_core, score_tokens

def main():
    docs, normal_docs, anomalous_docs = load_grammar()
    train_docs, test_docs = split_docs(normal_docs, anomalous_docs, seed=0)
    
    # Check 1: dataset size
    print(f"Check 1 - Dataset size: {len(docs)} docs ({len(normal_docs)} normal, {len(anomalous_docs)} anomalous)")
    assert len(docs) == 300 and len(normal_docs) == 270 and len(anomalous_docs) == 30
    
    # Check 2: label consistency
    for d in docs:
        has_anom = any(l == 1 for l in d['token_labels'])
        assert has_anom == (d['doc_label'] == 1), f"Doc {d['id']} inconsistent"
    print("Check 2 - Label consistency: PASS")
    
    # Check 3: token class balance
    total_tokens = sum(len(d['tokens']) for d in docs)
    total_anom = sum(sum(d['token_labels']) for d in docs)
    test_tokens = sum(len(d['tokens']) for d in test_docs)
    test_anom = sum(sum(d['token_labels']) for d in test_docs)
    print(f"Check 3 - Token balance: total {total_tokens} tokens, {total_anom} anomalous ({100*total_anom/total_tokens:.2f}%)")
    print(f"         Test: {test_tokens} tokens, {test_anom} anomalous ({100*test_anom/test_tokens:.2f}%)")
    
    # Check 5: split sizes
    print(f"Check 5 - Split: {len(train_docs)} train docs, {len(test_docs)} test docs")
    assert len(train_docs) == 135 and len(test_docs) == 165
    
    # Embed full dataset
    tokenizer, model, device = get_tokenizer_model()
    train_emb, train_mask = embed_docs(train_docs, tokenizer, model, device)
    test_emb, test_mask = embed_docs(test_docs, tokenizer, model, device)
    
    X_train, _ = flatten_masked(train_emb, train_mask)
    X_test, test_indices = flatten_masked(test_emb, test_mask)
    
    # Check 6: memory bank size
    print(f"Check 6 - Memory bank size: {X_train.shape[0]} tokens")
    
    # Check 7: embedding dim
    assert X_train.shape[1] == 768, f"Expected 768 dim, got {X_train.shape[1]}"
    print(f"Check 7 - Embedding dim: {X_train.shape[1]}")
    
    # Check 4: alignment coverage
    total_gold = sum(len(d['tokens']) for d in train_docs + test_docs)
    total_embedded = X_train.shape[0] + X_test.shape[0]
    coverage = total_embedded / total_gold
    print(f"Check 4 - Alignment coverage: {total_embedded}/{total_gold} = {coverage:.4f}")
    
    # Build labels
    test_token_labels = []
    doc_token_masks = []
    for doc_idx, doc in enumerate(test_docs):
        doc_token_masks.append(np.array([i[0] == doc_idx for i in test_indices]))
        test_token_labels.extend(doc['token_labels'])
    test_token_labels = np.array(test_token_labels, dtype=int)
    test_doc_labels = np.array([d['doc_label'] for d in test_docs], dtype=int)
    
    # Fit and score
    model_tok = fit_token_core(X_train)
    token_scores = score_tokens(model_tok, X_test)
    
    # Check 8: sanity baselines
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    rand_scores = rng.rand(test_token_labels.shape[0])
    rand_auroc = compute_token_metrics(rand_scores, test_token_labels)['token_auroc']
    print(f"Check 8a - Random baseline AUROC: {rand_auroc:.4f}")
    
    noise = rng.normal(0, 1e-6, X_train.shape).astype(np.float32)
    train_scores = score_tokens(model_tok, X_train + noise)
    max_self = float(np.max(train_scores))
    print(f"Check 8b - Max self-distance (train): {max_self:.6f}")
    
    # Check 9: metric parity on synthetic data
    from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score
    y_true = np.array([0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1])
    y_score = np.array([0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.8, 0.9, 0.7])
    manual_auroc = roc_auc_score(y_true, y_score)
    manual_auprc = average_precision_score(y_true, y_score)
    print(f"Check 9 - Metric parity: AUROC={manual_auroc:.4f}, AUPRC={manual_auprc:.4f}")
    
    # Final metrics
    token_m = compute_token_metrics(token_scores, test_token_labels)
    doc_scores = aggregate_doc_scores(token_scores, doc_token_masks)
    doc_m = compute_doc_metrics(doc_scores, test_doc_labels)
    print(f"\nFinal token AUROC: {token_m['token_auroc']:.4f}")
    print(f"Final token AUPRC: {token_m['token_auprc']:.4f}")
    print(f"Final doc AUROC: {doc_m['doc_auroc']:.4f}")
    print(f"Final doc AUPRC: {doc_m['doc_auprc']:.4f}")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import os
import sys
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))

from src.data_grammar import load_grammar, split_docs
from src.embed_bert import get_tokenizer_model, embed_docs, flatten_masked
from src.detector import fit_token_core, score_tokens
from src.evaluate import compute_token_metrics, compute_doc_metrics, aggregate_doc_scores
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score


def run_alternative(seed=0, metric='euclidean', n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max', per_doc_auroc=False):
    docs, normal_docs, anomalous_docs = load_grammar()
    train_docs, test_docs = split_docs(normal_docs, anomalous_docs, seed=seed)
    
    tokenizer, model, device = get_tokenizer_model()
    train_emb, train_mask = embed_docs(train_docs, tokenizer, model, device)
    test_emb, test_mask = embed_docs(test_docs, tokenizer, model, device)
    
    X_train, _ = flatten_masked(train_emb, train_mask)
    X_test, test_indices = flatten_masked(test_emb, test_mask)
    
    test_token_labels = []
    doc_token_masks = []
    for doc_idx, doc in enumerate(test_docs):
        doc_token_masks.append(np.array([i[0] == doc_idx for i in test_indices]))
        test_token_labels.extend(doc['token_labels'])
    test_token_labels = np.array(test_token_labels, dtype=int)
    test_doc_labels = np.array([d['doc_label'] for d in test_docs], dtype=int)
    
    # Fit with alternative settings
    nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=n_neighbors, metric=metric).fit(X_train)
    distances, _ = nbrs.kneighbors(X_test)
    if n_neighbors == 1:
        scores = distances.flatten()
    else:
        if aggregation == 'mean':
            scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
        elif aggregation == 'max':
            scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
        elif aggregation == 'min':
            scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
        elif aggregation == 'median':
            scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
        else:
            raise ValueError
    
    if per_doc_auroc:
        doc_aurocs = []
        doc_auprcs = []
        for mask in doc_token_masks:
            s = scores[mask]
            l = test_token_labels[mask]
            if len(np.unique(l)) > 1:
                doc_aurocs.append(roc_auc_score(l, s))
                doc_auprcs.append(average_precision_score(l, s))
            else:
                doc_aurocs.append(np.nan)
                doc_auprcs.append(np.nan)
        token_auroc = float(np.nanmean(doc_aurocs))
        token_auprc = float(np.nanmean(doc_auprcs))
    else:
        token_auroc = roc_auc_score(test_token_labels, scores)
        token_auprc = average_precision_score(test_token_labels, scores)
    
    doc_scores = aggregate_doc_scores(scores, doc_token_masks)
    doc_auroc = roc_auc_score(test_doc_labels, doc_scores)
    doc_auprc = average_precision_score(test_doc_labels, doc_scores)
    
    return token_auroc, token_auprc, doc_auroc, doc_auprc


if __name__ == '__main__':
    for metric in ['euclidean', 'cosine']:
        for per_doc in [False, True]:
            t_auc, t_prc, d_auc, d_prc = run_alternative(seed=0, metric=metric, per_doc_auroc=per_doc)
            print(f"metric={metric:10s} per_doc={str(per_doc):5s} -> token_auroc={t_auc:.4f} token_auprc={t_prc:.4f} doc_auroc={d_auc:.4f} doc_auprc={d_prc:.4f}")
    
    for k in [1, 3, 5]:
        for agg in ['mean', 'max']:
            t_auc, t_prc, d_auc, d_prc = run_alternative(seed=0, metric='euclidean', n_neighbors=k, aggregation=agg)
            print(f"k={k} agg={agg:5s} euclidean -> token_auroc={t_auc:.4f} token_auprc={t_prc:.4f} doc_auroc={d_auc:.4f} doc_auprc={d_prc:.4f}")

def get_tokenizer_model(model_name: str = "bert-base-uncased", device: str = None):
    if device is None:
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = model.to(device).eval()
    return tokenizer, model, device


def embed_with_align(
    docs: List[Dict],
    model_name: str = "bert-base-uncased",
    device: str = None,
    cache_path: str = None,
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, List[Tuple[int, int]]]:
    """
    Use the authors' extract_word_embeddings to get word-level embeddings.
    Returns:
        X_flat: (n_total_words, 768)
        labels_flat: (n_total_words,)
        indices: list of (doc_idx, word_idx) for each row
    """
    if cache_path and os.path.exists(cache_path):
        print(f"Loading cached embeddings from {cache_path}")
        data = np.load(cache_path, allow_pickle=True)
        return data['X_flat'], data['labels_flat'], data['indices'].tolist()
    
    tokenizer, model, device = get_tokenizer_model(model_name, device)
    
    all_tokens = [doc['tokens'] for doc in docs]
    all_labels = [doc['token_labels'] for doc in docs]
    
    # Suppress verbose prints from align.py
    f = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(f):
        train_data = extract_word_embeddings(
            model=model,
            tokenizer=tokenizer,
            all_tokens=all_tokens,
            all_labels=all_labels,
            model_name=model_name,
            device=device,
        )
    
    # Flatten
    X_flat = []
    labels_flat = []
    indices = []
    for doc_idx, sent in enumerate(train_data):
        for word_idx, item in enumerate(sent):
            X_flat.append(item['embedding'])
            labels_flat.append(item['label'])
            indices.append((doc_idx, word_idx))
    
    X_flat = np.array(X_flat, dtype=np.float32)
    labels_flat = np.array(labels_flat, dtype=int)
    
    if cache_path:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(cache_path), exist_ok=True)
        np.savez_compressed(
            cache_path,
            X_flat=X_flat,
            labels_flat=labels_flat,
            indices=np.array(indices, dtype=int),
        )
        print(f"Saved cached embeddings to {cache_path}")
    
    return X_flat, labels_flat, indices

import os
import sys
import numpy as np
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))

# Load cached embeddings
cache = np.load('cache/grammar_train_seed0.npz', allow_pickle=True)
X_train = cache['X_flat']
y_train = cache['labels_flat']

cache = np.load('cache/grammar_test_seed0.npz', allow_pickle=True)
X_test = cache['X_flat']
y_test = cache['labels_flat']

print(f"Train shape: {X_train.shape}, positive: {y_train.sum()}")
print(f"Test shape: {X_test.shape}, positive: {y_test.sum()}")

def test_config(X_train, X_test, y_test, metric='euclidean', normalize=False):
    if normalize:
        # L2 normalize each vector
        X_train_norm = X_train / (np.linalg.norm(X_train, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-8)
        X_test_norm = X_test / (np.linalg.norm(X_test, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-8)
        if metric == 'cosine':
            # Cosine distance on normalized vectors = euclidean distance
            nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1, metric='euclidean').fit(X_train_norm)
            dists, _ = nn.kneighbors(X_test_norm)
        else:
            nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1, metric='euclidean').fit(X_train_norm)
            dists, _ = nn.kneighbors(X_test_norm)
    else:
        if metric == 'cosine':
            # Use cosine distance directly
            nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1, metric='cosine').fit(X_train)
            dists, _ = nn.kneighbors(X_test)
        else:
            nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1, metric='euclidean').fit(X_train)
            dists, _ = nn.kneighbors(X_test)
    
    scores = dists.flatten()
    auroc = roc_auc_score(y_test, scores)
    auprc = average_precision_score(y_test, scores)
    return auroc, auprc

# Test configurations
configs = [
    ('uncased', 'euclidean', False),
    ('uncased', 'cosine', False),
    ('uncased', 'euclidean', True),
    ('uncased', 'cosine', True),
]

for bert_type, metric, normalize in configs:
    auroc, auprc = test_config(X_train, X_test, y_test, metric, normalize)
    print(f"{bert_type} | {metric} | norm={normalize}: AUROC={auroc:.4f}, AUPRC={auprc:.4f}")

# Also test with cased embeddings if we have them cached
cached_train = 'cache/grammar_train_seed0_cased.npz'
cached_test = 'cache/grammar_test_seed0_cased.npz'
if os.path.exists(cached_train) and os.path.exists(cached_test):
    X_train_c = np.load(cached_train)['X_flat']
    X_test_c = np.load(cached_test)['X_flat']
    for metric, normalize in [('euclidean', False), ('cosine', False), ('euclidean', True)]:
        auroc, auprc = test_config(X_train_c, X_test_c, y_test, metric, normalize)
        print(f"cased | {metric} | norm={normalize}: AUROC={auroc:.4f}, AUPRC={auprc:.4f}")
else:
    print("Cached cased embeddings not found")

import os
import sys
import numpy as np
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))

from src.data_grammar import load_grammar, split_docs

y_test_global = None

def test_seed(seed):
    global y_test_global
    docs, normal_docs, anomalous_docs = load_grammar()
    train_docs, test_docs = split_docs(normal_docs, anomalous_docs, seed=seed)
    
    train_cache = f'cache/grammar_train_seed{seed}_cased.npz'
    test_cache = f'cache/grammar_test_seed{seed}_cased.npz'
    
    if not os.path.exists(train_cache) or not os.path.exists(test_cache):
        print(f"Cache missing for seed {seed}")
        return
    
    X_train = np.load(train_cache)['X_flat']
    X_test = np.load(test_cache)['X_flat']
    y_test = np.load(test_cache)['labels_flat']
    y_test_global = y_test
    
    for metric in ['euclidean', 'cosine']:
        nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1, metric=metric).fit(X_train)
        dists, _ = nn.kneighbors(X_test)
        scores = dists.flatten()
        auroc = roc_auc_score(y_test, scores)
        auprc = average_precision_score(y_test, scores)
        print(f"seed={seed} cased {metric}: AUROC={auroc:.4f}, AUPRC={auprc:.4f}")

for seed in [0, 1, 2]:
    test_seed(seed)

import os
import sys
import numpy as np
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))

from src.data_grammar import load_grammar, split_docs
from src.detector import fit_token_core, score_tokens
from src.evaluate import compute_token_metrics, compute_doc_metrics, aggregate_doc_scores

def run_seed(seed, model_name='bert-base-uncased'):
    docs, normal_docs, anomalous_docs = load_grammar()
    train_docs, test_docs = split_docs(normal_docs, anomalous_docs, seed=seed)
    
    # Determine cache suffix based on model name
    if 'cased' in model_name:
        suffix = 'cased'
    else:
        suffix = 'uncased'
    
    train_cache = f'cache/grammar_train_seed{seed}_{suffix}.npz'
    test_cache = f'cache/grammar_test_seed{seed}_{suffix}.npz'
    
    X_train = np.load(train_cache)['X_flat']
    X_test = np.load(test_cache)['X_flat']
    y_test_tokens = np.load(test_cache)['labels_flat']
    
    # Assert embeddings differ between cased/uncased if both exist
    if 'cased' in model_name and os.path.exists(f'cache/grammar_train_seed{seed}_uncased.npz'):
        X_train_uncased = np.load(f'cache/grammar_train_seed{seed}_uncased.npz')['X_flat']
        assert not np.allclose(X_train, X_train_uncased), "Cached cased and uncased embeddings should differ!"
    
    # Fit TokenCore
    model = fit_token_core(X_train)
    token_scores = score_tokens(model, X_test)
    
    # Token metrics
    token_metrics = compute_token_metrics(token_scores, y_test_tokens)
    
    # Document metrics
    doc_token_masks = []
    idx = 0
    for doc in test_docs:
        n = len(doc['tokens'])
        mask = np.zeros(len(y_test_tokens), dtype=bool)
        mask[idx:idx+n] = True
        doc_token_masks.append(mask)
        idx += n
    
    doc_scores = aggregate_doc_scores(token_scores, doc_token_masks)
    doc_labels = np.array([doc['doc_label'] for doc in test_docs])
    doc_metrics = compute_doc_metrics(doc_scores, doc_labels)
    
    print(f"seed={seed} {model_name}: token_AUROC={token_metrics['token_auroc']:.4f}, token_AUPRC={token_metrics['token_auprc']:.4f}, doc_AUROC={doc_metrics['doc_auroc']:.4f}")
    return token_metrics, doc_metrics

print("=== bert-base-uncased ===")
for seed in [0, 1, 2]:
    run_seed(seed, 'bert-base-uncased')

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import numpy as np
from typing import Dict, List

# Ensure src is importable
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))

from src.data_grammar import load_grammar, split_docs
from src.detector import fit_token_core, score_tokens
from src.evaluate import compute_token_metrics, compute_doc_metrics, aggregate_doc_scores


def run_single_seed(seed: int, model_name: str = "bert-base-uncased") -> Dict:
    """Run TokenCore on Grammar dataset for a single seed."""
    docs, normal_docs, anomalous_docs = load_grammar()
    train_docs, test_docs = split_docs(normal_docs, anomalous_docs, seed=seed)
    
    # Determine cache suffix
    suffix = "cased" if "cased" in model_name else "uncased"
    train_cache = f"cache/grammar_train_seed{seed}_{suffix}.npz"
    test_cache = f"cache/grammar_test_seed{seed}_{suffix}.npz"
    
    # Load cached embeddings
    X_train = np.load(train_cache)["X_flat"]
    X_test = np.load(test_cache)["X_flat"]
    y_test_tokens = np.load(test_cache)["labels_flat"]
    
    # Fit TokenCore
    model = fit_token_core(X_train)
    token_scores = score_tokens(model, X_test)
    
    # Token metrics
    token_metrics = compute_token_metrics(token_scores, y_test_tokens)
    
    # Document metrics (mean aggregation)
    doc_token_masks = []
    idx = 0
    for doc in test_docs:
        n = len(doc["tokens"])
        mask = np.zeros(len(y_test_tokens), dtype=bool)
        mask[idx:idx + n] = True
        doc_token_masks.append(mask)
        idx += n
    
    doc_scores = aggregate_doc_scores(token_scores, doc_token_masks)
    doc_labels = np.array([doc["doc_label"] for doc in test_docs])
    doc_metrics = compute_doc_metrics(doc_scores, doc_labels)
    
    return {
        "seed": seed,
        "token_auroc": token_metrics["token_auroc"],
        "token_auprc": token_metrics["token_auprc"],

    docs, normal_docs, anomalous_docs = load_grammar()
    
    # Use 8 normal + 2 anomalous

def run_seed(seed):
    docs, normal_docs, anomalous_docs = load_grammar()
    train_docs, test_docs = split_docs(normal_docs, anomalous_docs, seed=seed)
    
    train_cache = f'cache/grammar_train_seed{seed}_uncased.npz'
    test_cache = f'cache/grammar_test_seed{seed}_uncased.npz'

    # Per-document AUROC averaged
    doc_aurocs = []
    idx = 0
    for doc in test_docs:
        n = len(doc['tokens'])
        if n == 0:

        scores = token_scores[idx:idx+n]
        labels = y_test_tokens[idx:idx+n]
        if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:

target.statement: TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar dataset
target.table_ref: Table 1, Token section, row TokenCore, column Grammar ROC

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The clean re-run of `python reproduce.py` fails with `NameError: name 'roc_auc_score' is not defined` (and the script also references `r["token_auroc"]` although the function returns `token_auroc_micro`), so results/metrics.json is null and the submitted 0.5978/0.6509 numbers are not reproduced by the delivered artifact. The design is aimed at the right target: Grammar, 50% normal training, BERT-base-uncased word embeddings, a normal-only memory bank, nearest-neighbor token scores, and mean document aggregation. However, the used embedding path is the external authors' `repo/align.extract_word_embeddings` and the detector is the authors' `repo/TokenCore`, so the exact max-pooling and distance metric cannot be audited from the submitted source; the six baselines are absent. Even the implementer's own primary micro AUROC 0.5978 is outside the ±0.02 band, while the per-document-average variant 0.6509 is inside, making the paper's unstated micro-vs-per-document token AUROC aggregation (A5) the main substantive divergence; distance/normalization/punctuation choices (A1, A3, A4, A9) and the random split (A8) add drift. The run is not scaled down (full Grammar, three seeds), but it is not reproducible as delivered until the script bugs are fixed and the clean run actually writes a metrics file.

requirement_check.evidence: reproduce.py and embed_bert_v2.py instantiate bert-base-uncased, so TokenCore uses the required backbone, but only TokenCore is run; the six baselines required by R1/R8 are absent. The max-pooling path is delegated to repo/align.extract_word_embeddings, which is not included in the submitted source files.

src/embed_bert.py contains an explicit element-wise np.max over subword embeddings, but reproduce.py does not use it; it uses src/embed_bert_v2.embed_with_align -> repo/align.extract_word_embeddings, whose max-pooling implementation is not visible in the audit bundle.

reproduce.run_single_seed calls split_docs, which returns train_docs containing only normal documents (135 of 270), and passes X_train from those documents to fit_token_core; no anomalous-token embeddings enter the memory bank.
src/evaluate.aggregate_doc_scores computes np.mean over each document's token scores, and reproduce.py uses that function for document-level AUROC/AUPRC.
src/data_grammar.split_docs sets n_train = len(normal_docs)//2 = 135 and test_docs = remaining 135 normal + all 30 anomalous, i.e. 50% of normal documents for training.

reproduce.py computes token AUROC/AUPRC both micro and per-document and document AUROC/AUPRC, but the clean re-run crashes before writing results/metrics.json; no metrics are actually reported by the delivered run.
No LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder or LUNAR implementation is present; only TokenCore is run.
Same as R2: word-level alignment is delegated to repo/align.extract_word_embeddings, not to the visible src/embed_bert.py max-pooling code used in the earlier exploratory scripts.
src/data_grammar.load_grammar asserts 300 total documents, 270 normal and 30 anomalous, loading repo/data/grammar.npy and repo/data/grammar_correction_labeled.json.
src/data_grammar.load_grammar asserts that doc_label == 1 iff at least one token label is 1, enforcing consistency between token-level and document-level labels.
